title: Hash tables
learn: hash functions, collisions (chaining/open addressing), load factor, average O(1) vs worst O(n), set vs map, `Counter`, `defaultdict`
hook: Hash maps are the single most useful tool in coding interviews: they turn "search the array again" into "look it up". Two Sum, the most famous interview question of all, is a hash map question.

explain.prompt: An interviewer asks: how does a hash table give O(1) lookups, and when does it stop being O(1)? Use Two Sum as your example.
keyPoints: a hash function maps a key to a bucket index, so a lookup jumps straight to one bucket
collisions (two keys, same bucket) are handled by chaining or open addressing
average O(1) insert/lookup/delete; worst case O(n) if many keys collide; resizing keeps the load factor low
Two Sum: store value → index while scanning and look up target − x: O(n) time, O(n) space vs O(n²) for all pairs
